claims.text: WHO Representative to Sudan Dr. Shible Sahbani reported more than 1,330 confirmed cholera cases and 114 confirmed deaths, a case fatality rate of 13.7 percent, in an outbreak affecting several states, mainly in the western part of the country, the Darfurs and the Kordofans, briefing journalists in Geneva on 10 July 2026. Aid officials say the true number of fatalities is likely much higher, and the disease is expected to spread further as the rainy season sets in, particularly among people who have fled towns and rural areas in North Kordofan.

Re-checked 8 August 2026: ECDC's cholera-monthly page still shows Sudan's most recent data cut as 12 July 2026 (1,511 cases, 153 deaths since 1 January 2026); no newer monthly update has been published for the current (27 June 2026-onward) outbreak.

Re-checked 9 August 2026: ECDC's cholera-monthly page (dated 27 July 2026) still shows Sudan's most recent data cut as 12 July 2026 (1,511 cumulative cases, 153 deaths since 1 January 2026); no newer monthly update has been published.

UN News report (14 July 2026), citing OCHA, reconfirms WHO's count of 1,330 confirmed cholera cases and 114 deaths as of 7 July 2026, and describes the outbreak's continued spread: new confirmed and suspected cases in Kalma/Kampala displacement camp (South Darfur) and Tawila (North Darfur); West Kordofan reporting the highest caseload with new suspected cases and deaths; and North Kordofan reporting 32 new suspected cases in Gharb Bara locality in a single day. WHO delivered 8.5 tonnes of medical supplies to Kadugli and Dilling, South Kordofan — its first shipment there since December 2024 — and UNICEF delivered health supplies to El Fula, West Kordofan, serving about 429,000 people.

WFP report (data as of 17 July 2026): regular power outages are disrupting water supplies in El Obeid, and more than 30 new cholera cases have been recorded there as the city's displacement and hunger crisis deepens.

UN Women statement (24 July 2026): 'Cholera is already spreading in Sudan, with 1,330 cases reported by WHO in early July,' confirming no revised national cumulative total has superseded the 7 July WHO count as of this date.

Re-checked 1 August 2026: no newer WHO or ReliefWeb figure supersedes the 10 July 2026 Geneva briefing count of 1,330+ confirmed cholera cases and 114 deaths (CFR 13.7%) in Sudan reported by WHO's Representative to Sudan; WHO's global multi-country cholera epidemiological update series has not published a newer Sudan-specific count as of this check.

Re-checked 2 August 2026: WHO's national aggregate (1,330+ cases, 114 deaths, reported 10 July) remains the latest published figure; no newer WHO epidemiological update for Sudan cholera has been found, and the outbreak has not been declared contained.

WHO Multi-country outbreak of cholera, Epidemiological Update no. 38 (published 30 June 2026, data as of 31 May 2026): 'Sudan' is listed under the Eastern Mediterranean Region reporting 527 cumulative cholera cases and 61 deaths (CFR 11.6%) for 1 January to 31 May 2026, with 518 cases and 61 deaths (CFR 11.8%) in the preceding 28 days. This multi-country surveillance figure is dated to 31 May 2026 and is superseded chronologically by the 1,330-case/114-death figure WHO's Representative to Sudan reported on 10 July 2026 for the same national outbreak; re-checked 5 August 2026, no WHO or ReliefWeb Sudan-specific update newer than the 10 July figure has been published, and no allowlisted source has declared the outbreak contained.

ECDC's cholera-monthly page (updated 27 July 2026) reports for Sudan: 'Since 11 January 2026 and as of 12 July 2026, 1 502 new cases, including 153 new deaths' and, year-to-date, 'Since 1 January 2026 and as of 12 July 2026, 1 511 cases, including 153 deaths' — compared with 32,230 cases and 774 deaths in the equivalent 2025 timeframe (1 January-8 July 2025). This is a later data cutoff (12 July 2026) than WHO's Representative to Sudan's 10 July 2026 Geneva briefing figure (1,330 cases, 114 deaths) and is treated here as the most current published national aggregate.

Re-checked 7 August 2026 via direct fetch: ECDC's cholera-monthly page is still last updated 27 July 2026, and continues to report for Sudan, since 1 January 2026 and as of 12 July 2026: '1,511 cases, including 153 deaths' -- identical to the figures on file. No newer ECDC or WHO update was found.

description: Sudan's third cholera wave in as many years has spread across war-affected western and central states, principally Darfur and Kordofan, where conflict and constrained humanitarian access are hampering the response. WHO warns the outbreak could worsen further as the rainy season sets in and displacement continues around besieged cities such as El Obeid, where WFP reported more than 30 additional cases in mid-July. ECDC's cholera-monthly surveillance page (updated 27 July 2026, data as of 12 July 2026) now records a higher national cumulative total of 1,511 cases and 153 deaths since 1 January 2026 (CFR ~10.1%), superseding the WHO Representative to Sudan's 10 July briefing figure (1,330 cases, 114 deaths, CFR 13.7%) as the most current confirmed national aggregate. Continued geographic spread has been reported into new localities in North and West Kordofan and South Darfur. A separate, earlier WHO multi-country cholera epidemiological update (data as of 31 May 2026, published 30 June) recorded a lower cumulative Sudan figure of 527 cases and 61 deaths for 1 January-31 May 2026 under its own multi-country surveillance stream; that update predates and does not supersede the more recent figures. Re-checked 8 August 2026: ECDC's cholera-monthly page still shows Sudan's most recent data cut as 12 July 2026 (1,511 cases, 153 deaths since 1 January 2026); no newer monthly update has been published for the current (27 June 2026-onward) outbreak. Re-checked 9 August 2026: ECDC's cholera-monthly page (dated 27 July 2026) still reports Sudan's most recent data cut as 12 July 2026 (1,511 cases, 153 deaths since 1 January 2026); no newer ECDC update or WHO multi-country cholera epidemiological update (still #38, 30 June 2026) has been published.

impact.summary: ECDC's cholera-monthly surveillance page (updated 27 July 2026) reports that, since 1 January 2026 and as of 12 July 2026, Sudan recorded 1,511 cumulative cholera cases including 153 deaths (implied case fatality rate ~10.1%) — of which 1,502 cases and 153 deaths occurred since 11 January 2026 alone. This is the most current published national aggregate as of 6 August 2026, superseding WHO's Representative to Sudan's 10 July 2026 Geneva briefing figure (more than 1,330 confirmed cases and 114 deaths, CFR 13.7%) in an outbreak affecting several western and central Sudanese states, mainly Darfur and Kordofan. WFP reported in mid-July that more than 30 additional cholera cases had been recorded specifically in El Obeid, North Kordofan, as power outages disrupt water supplies there. OCHA reporting describes active geographic spread into Kalma/Kampala displacement camp (South Darfur), Tawila (North Darfur), West Kordofan and North Kordofan, as WHO and UNICEF scale up medical supply deliveries to Kadugli, Dilling and El Fula. Aid officials say the true toll is likely higher, and WHO warns the outbreak could worsen as the rainy season continues and conflict constrains the humanitarian response. WHO's separate multi-country cholera epidemiological update #38 (published 30 June 2026, data as of 31 May 2026) recorded 527 Sudan cases and 61 deaths (CFR 11.6%) for 1 January-31 May 2026 through its own multi-country surveillance stream — an earlier data cut that predates and does not supersede the newer figures. No allowlisted source has declared the outbreak contained. Re-checked 7 August 2026: ECDC's cholera-monthly page remains last updated 27 July 2026, with Sudan figures unchanged (1,511 cases, 153 deaths, data as of 12 July 2026); no newer ECDC or WHO update has been published. Re-checked 8 August 2026: ECDC's cholera-monthly page still shows Sudan's most recent data cut as 12 July 2026 (1,511 cases, 153 deaths since 1 January 2026); no newer monthly update has been published for the current (27 June 2026-onward) outbreak. Re-checked 9 August 2026: ECDC's cholera-monthly page (dated 27 July 2026) still reports Sudan's most recent data cut as 12 July 2026 (1,511 cases, 153 deaths since 1 January 2026); no newer ECDC update or WHO multi-country cholera epidemiological update (still #38, 30 June 2026) has been published.
